answer: At dawn, agents bidding for dune restoration work must lock a $100 bond per identity for 30 days. Creating 1,000 fake bidders therefore ties up $100,000; splitting one wallet into many does not reduce the total bond required. This makes a sybil swarm costly even if its accounts do nothing: the attacker loses access to that capital for a month. If demand hits its nadir, idle fake identities still bear the same capital cost.
